report:
### Conclusion
**Yes.** Robust evidence from clinical trials and systematic reviews demonstrates that offering HIV self-testing (HIVST) as an additional strategy significantly increases overall HIV testing uptake compared to standard clinical testing services alone.

### Key Evidence
* **Doubled Testing Rates:** A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials found that HIVST approximately doubled HIV testing uptake relative to standard testing services (Risk Ratio: 2.09; 95% CI: 1.69–2.58).
* **Broader Reach:** The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends HIV self-testing as an additional strategy because it removes privacy and accessibility barriers, effectively reaching first-time testers, men, and key populations who may avoid facility-based care.
* **Secondary Distribution Success:** Providing self-tests to individuals to pass to their sexual partners or peers (secondary distribution) substantially increases partner testing rates compared to standard referral methods.

While self-testing significantly expands access and testing frequency, public health guidance notes that any reactive self-test result requires confirmatory clinical testing and linkage to HIV prevention or treatment services.

### Sources
* *EClinicalMedicine* meta-analysis on HIV self-testing uptake: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2589537021002716
* WHO guidance on HIV self-testing optimization: https://www.who.int/news/item/22-07-2023-who-recommends-optimizing-hiv-testing-services
* *The Lancet Global Health* report on secondary distribution: https://www.thelancet.com/journals/langlo/article/PIIS2214-109X(21)00257-6/fulltext
